What does the consultation cost, and what happens in it?
$175 for Texas residents, $250 from out of state, with a $100 deposit that holds the date and comes off the fee. The hour is with Dr. Stone, and you leave knowing your options and their costs.
How much time will I need away from work?
About a week after eyelid surgery, about ten days after CO2 laser resurfacing, two weeks after a facelift. Plan for one to two weeks and come back early if recovery allows.
, CareCredit and Scratchpay, and is a preferred provider with all major dental and medical carriers where a procedure is covered. Or a membership, which banks credit rather than borrowing it.

pages.seoDescription: The full surgical procedure, with muscle repair and skin removal, for a neck that has gone past what a suture can hold. $11,000 in Westlake, TX.

props.text: The full surgical procedure, with muscle repair and skin removal, for a neck that has gone past what a suture can hold.
$18,000 with the face, planned and performed together
A neck lift is not a skin operation.
Three layers have changed, and a result that lasts addresses all three in the same sitting. The one people expect to hear about is the least of them.
The sheet of muscle that gives the neck its shape, repaired where it has separated. This is the layer that holds.
Where the muscle is lax but the skin still has tone, a suture suspension may be enough: the MyEllevate
Contoured under the chin and along the jaw, so the border the muscle repair creates has a clean line to sit against.
Fullness under the chin is sometimes fat, sometimes muscle, sometimes both. Which it is on you is measured at the consultation.
Removed where it is genuinely in excess, rather than redraped over the problem.
The last layer, and the one everybody names first. Pulling it tight on its own is why work that has been done looks done.
The test is whether the skin takes up when you lift your chin.
This is the operation for real skin excess. If the skin retracts when the chin is raised, a suspension may still be enough. If it hangs, it needs removing.
Which of these sound like you?
Loose skin that does not take up when the chin is raised
Vertical banding down the front of the neck, visible at rest as well as when speaking
A jawline that has lost its border entirely rather than softened
Significant weight loss that has left the neck with more skin than it needs
Tick whichever apply. Nothing here is stored or sent.

Under the chin, then around and behind the ears.

Through a small incision under the chin the platysma is repaired in the midline where it has separated and the fat is contoured. Through incisions around and behind the ears, in the natural creases, the skin is redraped and the excess removed.
Scars sit where the anatomy conceals them and mature over months from pink to pale. Scar care starts as soon as the wounds are closed.
A drain is sometimes used for the first day or two, and comes out at the first post-operative visit.

A support garment, swelling and tightness. Day three is the worst of it and it improves quickly after that.
Sutures out, back at a desk
Sutures come out in stages across the first two weeks. Most people are back at a desk at two weeks and comfortable in company shortly after.
The result keeps refining as swelling resolves and the tissues soften. Follow-ups are with Dr. Stone herself.
The first fortnight is at home.
By month three most people have stopped thinking about it.

The marginal mandibular nerve runs exactly where a neck lift works. A surgeon has to know it in three dimensions, in a particular neck, under tension. Dr. Stone spent her residency rebuilding it after it had been broken, and that is the background she brings to an elective neck.

Under the chin, and around and behind the ears in the natural creases, where the anatomy conceals them. They mature over months from pink to pale.

pages.seoTitle: Blepharoplasty Westlake TX | Stone Surgical Arts
pages.seoDescription: Eyelid surgery, upper or lower, by Dr. Mona Stone. An hour or less in the chair and seven to ten days off work. $3,400 in Westlake, TX.

props.text: Eyelid surgery, upper or lower. The smallest operation on this list and, for most faces, the one that changes the most.
Upper or lower, as the practice's own price list quotes it
Three tissues, and the skin is only the first of them.
The practice describes the upper lid operation in one sentence: excess skin, muscle and fat, removed and repositioned. Most people come for the first. The last usually changes the most.
The fat behind the muscle, pushing forward as the tissue holding it back gives way. It is what a bag under the eye is made of.
Modern technique increasingly repositions this fat into the hollow beneath the eye rather than removing it. Removal is how a lid ends up hollow instead of rested.
A strip of the muscle that circles the eye, addressed where it contributes to the fold, through the same opening as the skin.
The layer nobody asks about, and why two lids with the same skin removed can settle differently.
The fold on the crease, on the lashes, or in marked cases in the outer field of vision. The layer everybody names first.
On the lower lid it punishes over-resection hardest: take too much and the lid pulls away from the eye.
The test is what happens when the brow is held where it used to sit.
Lift the tail of your brow with a fingertip. If that millimetre opens the eye, you need a brow lift, not this. If the eye stays heavy with the brow up, the weight is in the lid.
Which of these sound like you?
Upper lid skin that folds over the crease, or sits on the lashes
Bags or puffiness there the moment you wake, not only after a bad night
Hollowing beneath the eye that makes cheek and lid read as two structures
Eye makeup that no longer sits on the upper lid because there is nowhere flat for it
Tick whichever apply. Nothing here is stored or sent.

htmlAttributes.data-r1: One sign on its own settles nothing, and the brow test above settles more than any of them. It is worth an hour with Dr. Stone to find out which of the two operations you are actually looking at.
htmlAttributes.data-r2: Two of the four is the usual reason people book. Bring them to a consultation; the answer may still be the brow rather than the lid.
htmlAttributes.data-r3: Three of the four is the pattern this operation is for, though whether it is the upper lid, the lower, or both is decided on examination and not from a list.
htmlAttributes.data-r4: All four is the picture this page describes. It is still Dr. Stone's examination that says whether it is a blepharoplasty, a brow lift, or the two planned together.

props.text: Where the real problem is a descended brow resting on the lid, the answer is a brow and forehead lift at $5,000–7,000. Dr. Stone will show you the difference at the consultation.
In the crease above, and beneath the lash line below.
On the upper lid the incision sits in the natural crease and disappears once healed. Excess skin, muscle and fat are removed or repositioned through that one opening.
On the lower lid it goes just beneath the lash line, or inside the lid where only fat is being addressed, which leaves no external scar.

It is an outpatient operation of an hour or less, under local anaesthetic with sedation or a general where the work or the patient calls for it. The practice uses a long-acting local that can carry pain relief for forty to seventy two hours, so most patients need nothing stronger at home. A platelet rich plasma or platelet rich fibrin treatment can be added during the procedure to help the site heal.
A morning, a week of bruising, and a lid that keeps settling.
The shortest recovery on the practice's surgical list. The figures are conventional ranges. Dr. Stone will give you the numbers for your own lids.
An hour or less, and home the same day
One to two hours if upper and lower lids are done together. Somebody else drives: sedation rules it out for twenty four hours.
Cold compresses and sleeping propped up shorten it considerably. Tenderness, watering, light sensitivity and some blurring from the ointment are all normal.
At around a week. Most of the healing happens inside the first fortnight and most people are back to normal activities within it.
Comfortable in company, then in photographs
Comfortable in company at ten days, in photographs at three weeks. The last swelling resolves over two to three months and the scar keeps fading past that.
The bruising week is at home, and it is a week.
By three weeks most people have stopped avoiding cameras.
Three different answers to "something about my eyes".
These are not three sizes of the same operation. One works above the eye, one on the lid, one on the surface of the skin, and it is common to need two. Each is quoted separately.
The upper third of the face, compared. Fees are the practice's own.
A brow that has descended onto the lid, and the muscles pulling it down
Excess lid skin, and the fat that has come forward behind it
The surface only: fine crepe, pigment and texture on thin lid skin
In the scalp and hairline, above the problem
In the upper crease, or beneath the lash line, or inside the lid
Five to ten days of social downtime
Dermal filler is a fourth conversation: it can soften a hollow under the eye at $800 a syringe, but it removes no skin and repositions no fat, so it does nothing for a heavy lid.
A lower lid gives back nothing that is taken from it in error.

Lower lids punish over-resection: take too much skin or fat and the lid pulls away from the eye, which is difficult to correct. Dr. Stone trained in oral and maxillofacial surgery across three Level 1 trauma centres, where the orbit and the tissues around it are rebuilt after injury. That is the background she brings to an elective lid.

In the upper crease, where it disappears once healed. On the lower lid, just beneath the lash line, or inside the lid where only fat is addressed, which leaves no external scar.

The practice puts eyelid surgery at ten to fifteen years or more, and upper lid surgery is a once in a lifetime operation for most patients. You continue to age, but the tissue removed does not come back, though some choose to repeat it later for new sagging.

Occasionally, for upper lids only, where excess skin is documented to obstruct the visual field. That needs formal visual field testing and photographs. It is a question for your insurer, and most cases are cosmetic.
Can filler or laser do this instead?

They address different things. Filler can soften a hollow under the eye, laser can improve the texture of thin lid skin, and for early changes either may be enough. Neither removes excess skin or repositions fat.

When the heaviness is the brow rather than the lid, the lift belongs above the eye. $5,000 to $7,000.
Hollowing under the eye is volume, not skin, and is answered with your own fat rather than a knife.
Fine lines on the lid and the crow’s feet beside it, where surgery removes nothing. $2,000 to $2,800.

The comparisons people get stuck on.
or a neck lift: how do I know which?
A neck lift uses small incisions behind the ears and under the chin, and can last up to ten years. MyEllevate
places internal sutures through small punctures, and lasts around five. MyEllevate
suits earlier laxity; a neck lift reverses advanced sagging, wrinkling or fullness. MyEllevate
also needs only local anaesthetic, so you can drive yourself home.
Will a neck lift fix my jowls?
No, and it is the most common mix-up. Jowls sit low, so people assume neck work, but they originate in sagging facial tissue. A minimally invasive facelift is the procedure that reduces them.

Fillers are gel injectables that plump and smooth lines, acne scars and thin lips, lasting months to a couple of years by product and site. Implants are customised, biocompatible inserts that reshape the structure beneath and stay intact, so the contour is permanent. Filler changes the surface, an implant the frame.
How long does each result actually last?
The practice’s published figures: blepharoplasty 10–15 years or more; a neck lift up to ten; MyEllevate

around five; facial implants and buccal fat reduction permanent, though significant weight gain can return fullness to the cheek elsewhere. Injectables are months, not years: maintenance, not surgery.
Can I have more than one procedure at once?

Often, and frequently the better plan: a neck lift alongside a facelift or eyelid surgery means one recovery instead of two. What combines safely depends on your anatomy and time under anaesthetic, decided at the consultation.
Why do some rows say “at consultation” instead of a price?
Because the practice never published a figure for those, and we would rather show a gap than a guess. Genioplasty, fat transfer and facelift fees vary with the case, as the practice’s own pages say.
